transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I suppose it’s this driving thing, mostly. I hate to make too much of it, but when my car gets to one of those long bridges going toward Miami, I just… my chest tightens right up, and my hands grip the wheel so hard. All at once I feel absolutely sure I need to get off the bridge, even though of course there’s nowhere to go. It’s embarrassing to say, but that’s what finally made me think I should talk to someone.
Do you get this same feeling in other places where it might be hard to get away, like tunnels, elevators, or crowded stores?

Not really in those places, at least not that I’ve noticed. It’s mainly the bridges. The minute my car gets onto one of those long bridges toward Miami, I just tighten up—my chest, my hands on the wheel—and I get this awful sudden feeling that I have to get off, even though I know I can’t. I know that probably sounds a bit silly.
When you’re not on a bridge, do you ever have these attacks out of the blue?
I don’t think so, no. At least, I can’t recall it happening just out of nowhere. It seems to be tied to the bridge situation, if that’s the right way to put it.
When you’re on a bridge, what are you most afraid will happen?

I suppose… I’m afraid of being out there over all that open water and something going wrong, though I know that doesn’t make much sense. Those bridges have been there forever, and people drive over them every day just fine. But in the moment, the danger feels much bigger than it probably is.
If someone else is driving, do you still feel this fear when crossing a bridge?

Yes… I think I do, though it’s maybe a little less embarrassing when I’m not the one holding the wheel. But the fear is still there. The moment the car gets onto one of those long bridges toward Miami, I feel my chest tighten, and I just get this sudden feeling like, “I need to get off this bridge,” even though of course there’s nowhere to go. Does that make sense?
Outside of bridges, do you avoid any other situations because escape might be difficult?
Not that I can think of, no. I don’t really avoid places just because it would be hard to get out. It’s mostly the bridges that seem to do it. I hope that’s answering what you mean.
Do you avoid crossing bridges because of this fear?

Yes… I do, more than I’d like to admit. I tell myself it’s just being “practical,” but I’ve started turning down things like gallery openings or birdwatching trips, and even some visits with my daughter, unless someone else can drive me over those bridges. I’m embarrassed to say that, because I’ve always been the one who planned things and managed on my own. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
